docs.title: Create a Payment Intent
docs.text: The POST /v1/payment_intents endpoint creates a new Payment Intent object to track the lifecycle of a customer checkout session.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
This endpoint requires a Bearer token in the authorization header. Authorization: Bearer <sk_live_token>

Alternative Authentication Methods

Depending on your integration type, you can also authenticate using:

  • Basic Auth: Use your secret API key as the username and leave the password blank.
  • OAuth 2.0: Required if your application is acting on behalf of another user. Use the Authorization: Bearer <oauth_token> header.

docs.title: Body Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description amount integer Yes The amount to charge, represented in the smallest currency unit (e.g., cents). currency string Yes Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase. payment_method string No The ID of the payment method to attach to this Payment Intent. receipt_email string No Email address where the receipt should be sent upon successful payment.

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text:
• 400 Bad Request: Missing required parameters.
  • 401 Unauthorized: Invalid or missing API key.

docs.title: Microsystem Integration Architecture
docs.text: This guide outlines the event-driven architecture used to synchronize data across our primary microsystems: the User Service, the Billing Service, and the Notification Service.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: To prevent tight coupling between distinct domains, our backend relies on an asynchronous, event-driven architecture using Apache Kafka as the central message broker. This ensures that a failure in the Notification Service does not impact the critical path of the Billing Service.

docs.title: Core Components
docs.text:
1. API Gateway: The single entry point for all client requests. It handles rate limiting, authentication, and request routing.
  2. User Service: Manages identity, profile data, and access control.
  3. Billing Service: Processes transactions and generates invoices.
  4. Kafka Event Bus: The centralized streaming platform that routes domain events (e.g., user.created, invoice.paid) to subscribed services.

docs.title: Event Flow: Account Creation
docs.text:
When a new user registers, the system executes the following flow:

  1. The client sends a POST /register request to the API Gateway.
  2. The Gateway routes the payload to the User Service.
  3. The User Service commits the new user record to its dedicated database.
  4. The User Service publishes a user.created event to the Kafka Event Bus.
  5. The Billing Service consumes the event and provisions a billing profile for the user.
  6. The Notification Service consumes the event and dispatches a welcome email.

docs.title: Design Considerations
docs.text:
• Eventual Consistency: Because services operate asynchronously, there is a slight delay (typically under 50ms) before the Billing Service recognizes a newly created user. Client applications must be designed to handle this brief propagation window.
  • Database per Service: Each microsystem maintains its own independent database schema. Direct cross-database queries are strictly prohibited to maintain domain isolation.

docs.title: 🚀 New Features
docs.text:
• Webhooks Dashboard: You can now monitor webhook delivery statuses, view request payloads, and manually retry failed events directly from the Developer Console.
  • Idempotency Keys: The Payments API now supports Idempotency-Key headers to safely retry requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice.

docs.title: 🐛 Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• Data Migration: Resolved an issue where legacy database migrations from Oracle to SQL Server occasionally dropped the timestamp column on batched uploads.
  • Authentication: Fixed a token-refresh bug that caused active sessions to timeout prematurely after 24 hours instead of the configured 48 hours.

docs.title: ⚠️ Deprecations
docs.text:
• The GET /v1/charges endpoint is now officially deprecated. Please migrate to the GET /v1/payment_intents endpoint by Q1 2027.

Important Release Notices

Please review the following items before deploying version 2.4.0 to your production environment:

  1. Known Issue & Workaround: If your Oracle to SQL Server migration hangs at 99% during a batched upload, manually restarting the background worker service will force the final commit to execute. A permanent fix is scheduled for v2.4.1.
  2. Upcoming Deprecation: The GET /v1/charges endpoint will be fully retired in the next major release (expected Q1 2027). Please migrate your integration to GET /v1/payment_intents to prevent future service disruptions.
  3. Phased Rollout: The new Webhooks Dashboard is currently rolling out gradually across all server regions. If you do not see the dashboard in your Developer Console today, it will be available by Friday.
  4. Pro Tip (Faster Bulk Uploads): With the new batching engine introduced in this release, you can now send up to 1,000 records per API request instead of 100. Update your payload limits to take advantage of the reduced latency.
